s1.syndrome_frame: Chronic eye symptoms with progressive vision loss and conjunctival abnormalities
key_facts: Initial visual acuity was 20/20 OD and 20/30 OS
Vision deteriorated to 20/30 OD and counting fingers OS over time
Slit lamp examination revealed subconjunctival fibrosis
Slit lamp examination revealed symblepharon formation
Slit lamp examination revealed corneal neovascularizations
Slit lamp examination revealed conjunctival hyperemia
Conjunctival biopsy and immunofluorescent histology revealed an unspecific result
Patient underwent therapy with reduction in conjunctival hyperemia and corneal vascularizations

raw.syndrome_frame: Chronic eye symptoms with progressive vision loss and conjunctival abnormalities
key_facts: Initial visual acuity was 20/20 OD and 20/30 OS
Vision deteriorated to 20/30 OD and counting fingers OS over time
Slit lamp examination revealed subconjunctival fibrosis
Slit lamp examination revealed symblepharon formation
Slit lamp examination revealed corneal neovascularizations

Patient underwent therapy with reduction in conjunctival hyperemia and corneal vascularizations

raw.rationale: The presence of subconjunctival fibrosis, symblepharon formation, and corneal neovascularizations are characteristic findings in Ocular Cicatricial Pemphigoid, which is a chronic autoimmune disorder that can lead to progressive vision loss.

rejected.label: Mucous Membrane Pemphigoid
rejected.why: While it shares some similar symptoms, Mucous Membrane Pemphigoid typically involves other mucous membranes beyond the eyes, which is not mentioned in the vignette.

rejected.label: Vernal Keratoconjunctivitis
rejected.why: This condition is more common in younger patients and typically presents with seasonal exacerbations, which is not indicated in the vignette.

rejected.label: Sarcoidosis
rejected.why: Sarcoidosis can cause uveitis and other ocular symptoms, but the specific findings of subconjunctival fibrosis and symblepharon formation are more characteristic of Ocular Cicatricial Pemphigoid.

rejected.label: Sjögren's Syndrome
rejected.why: While Sjögren's Syndrome can cause dry eye and other ocular symptoms, it does not typically cause the specific findings of subconjunctival fibrosis, symblepharon formation, and corneal neovascularizations seen in this patient.
